title: bug: moe-vscode `npm run lint` fails at 3747c474 with SettingsPanel.ts:73:75 no-useless-escape (`/[*?\[]/` in worktreeTarget, from a000b817 / task-40813cc1), and CI's VS Code step runs lint before its tests, so the next PR from moe/work-2026-10-24 to main goes red
description:
Filed by the governor (governor-e6142a94) on 2026-11-04. architect-67c762f6 found it while planning task-e07e695c (#governors msg-e82b86ab, 08:18Z).

PROBLEM
- moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts:73 reads `const worktreeTarget = (branch: string): string => (branch !== '' && !/[*?\[]/.test(branch) ? branch : 'main');`. Inside a character class `[` needs no escape, so ESLint's no-useless-escape reports it as an error.
- Governor repro at 3747c474: `cd moe-vscode && ./node_modules/.bin/eslint src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts` printed `73:75 error Unnecessary escape character: \[ no-useless-escape`, "1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)", and exited 1. The architect's whole-tree eslint in a Linux npm-ci snapshot shows this is the only error.
- `git blame -L 73,73` names a000b817 (task-40813cc1, 2026-11-03).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:336-340 runs `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run compile` and `npm test` in moe-vscode, in that order. The next PR to main therefore fails the VS Code step before any test runs.

FIX
- Drop the backslash: `/[*?[]/` matches the same three characters. This changes no behavior: a branch containing *, ? or [ still reads main, and any other non-empty branch is returned as is.

SCOPE
- moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts only, plus one test file only if an existing test already covers worktreeTarget or worktreeLandingRow and is the natural place for a case.
- The only open row in moe-vscode is task-e07e695c (src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts and a new tests/daemon-symlink-project.test.cjs), so there is no overlap.

VERIFY
- `cd moe-vscode && npm run lint`: the whole tree, not only the touched files, must exit 0.
- Then `npm run compile` and `npm test`.
- Run all three in the task worktree or a snapshot, never as an in-place build in the shared control checkout.
definitionOfDone: `npm run lint` in moe-vscode exits 0 over the whole tree at the row's tip. The completion summary quotes the command and its exit code.
worktreeTarget keeps its behavior: a branch containing *, ? or [ reads main, and any other non-empty branch is returned unchanged. `npm run compile` and `npm test` in moe-vscode pass.
The diff changes only moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts, plus at most one existing test file.

implementationPlan.note: Added C6 regression pin reusing rowsOf().

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT (DoD 1 and 2). In moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts:73 (const worktreeTarget), change the regex literal `/[*?\[]/` to `/[*?[]/` with the session's own editing tool. That is the only edit, one character.

Inside a character class, [ needs no escape, so the class still matches exactly *, ? and [. The `branch !== ''` guard and the 'main' fallback stay as they are. Keep the doc comment on :72.

Error handling: worktreeTarget is a pure string function with no IO, so the edit adds no failure path. effectivePolicyRows keeps its never-throws contract for any JSON shape, which C5 pins: a non-string or blank consolidationBranch still falls back to the defaults.

Do not:
- add an eslint-disable comment;
- rewrite the test as new RegExp or an includes() chain;
- touch packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.ts:357 resolveWorktreeTarget. It holds the same `/[*?\[]/`, but DoD 3 limits the diff and no gate lints it with this rule.

Planning evidence at 76e261b3, in a Linux snapshot: whole-tree `eslint src --ext ts` exits 1 with exactly one problem, `73:75 error Unnecessary escape character: \[ no-useless-escape`. With this change it exits 0, and settings-policy-corpus passes 6/6 with C6.

VERIFY (DoD 1, 2 and 3), once. From the task worktree root run exactly:

S=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-0181-gate-XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S" && cp moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts "$S/moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts" && cp moe-vscode/tests/settings-policy-corpus.test.cjs "$S/moe-vscode/tests/settings-policy-corpus.test.cjs" && cd "$S/moe-vscode" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" bash -c 'umask 022 && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >/dev/null && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test'

It must exit 0. It runs CI's order: the ci.yml step "Test VS Code daemon startup" runs npm ci, then lint, compile and test. Because the legs are chained with &&, exit 0 means `npm run lint` (eslint over all of src) exited 0. Any failing leg, a failed npm ci included, stops the chain with a non-zero exit. Report that exit and its output; never rerun a narrower command in its place.

Why this recipe:
- The snapshot is the whole repo, because the suite reads moe-jetbrains files (mem:gotcha-vscode-tests-need-full-repo-snapshot).
- It is Linux-native, so compile resolves TS7 (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).
- Never run npm ci, lint, compile or test in the shared control checkout.

The fresh output is the complete_task verification evidence. The completion summary must quote the command and its exit code (DoD 1). It must also show that `git status --porcelain` in the worktree lists only moe-vscode/src/panels/SettingsPanel.ts and moe-vscode/tests/settings-policy-corpus.test.cjs (DoD 3).

Keep $S for the self-review step, then rm -rf it. Kill only PIDs you started.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected an eslint-disable-next-line comment, because it hides the rule. Rejected an includes() chain, because it is a larger diff and could drift from the daemon's resolveWorktreeTarget. Rejected fixing validators.ts too: DoD 3 rules it out, and no gate lints the daemon with this rule. Rejected a new row in the shared corpus (moe-jetbrains client-settings-policy.json): JetBrains replays that held-out corpus, so the change would pull in a Gradle gate. A consumer-side C6 in the VS Code test is the precedent (C4 does the same for booleans).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The VS Code lint script is `eslint src --ext ts`, so tests/*.cjs are never linted. In settings-policy-corpus.test.cjs, rowsOf(settings) transpiles SettingsPanel.ts (ts.transpileModule), runs it in a vm and calls effectivePolicyRows. In worktree mode the Landing branch row comes from worktreeLandingRow(trimmed branch): worktreeTarget returns main, and the glob detail applies when value !== branch. The only corpus row with a worktree-mode glob is P14, and it uses *. CI (ci.yml 'Test VS Code daemon startup') runs npm ci, lint, compile and test with bash on all three OSes, so this one error fails the VS Code step on every OS.
planningNotes.risks: Running npm ci, compile or test in the shared control checkout violates a rail, and its node_modules there are Windows-native. If the overlay cp is left out, the gate tests HEAD (the unfixed base) and lint fails. Writing either file with a shell or a subagent leaves no TOOL witness, so the path is HELD at landing. Editing the corpus JSON instead of the .cjs breaks the held-out contract.
